_readme: Retrieval-side sweep: query-side settings ONLY, no re-ingest, one frozen corpus.
Why this file exists: the earlier conclusions about TOP_K, CHUNK_TOP_K, rerank and the
token budget were measured on a corpus smaller than what retrieval already returns, so
every arm saw nearly the whole store and 'no difference' was the only possible result
(docs/research/graphraggle-adversarial-review.md, F5 and 'Conclusions we should stop
trusting'). Fix the instrument first: run this with the retrieval-recall probe on
(--no-retrieval-recall to switch it off) so each arm reports evidence_in_context% -
whether the gold quote was in the context at all - separately from whether the answer
was right. Pair the two arms you care about with --compare.
Run it on the SECOND STACK, never on production. This file sets reingest:false on every
arm, so it does not delete anything, but it does rewrite <root>/.env and restart
containers while it runs:
.venv/bin/python scripts/overnight_loop.py \
--root ~/rag-project --out ~/rag-project/docs/ops/runs/retrieval-sweep \
--experiments docs/ops/loop/experiments-retrieval-sweep.json \
--lightrag-url http://127.0.0.1:9622 --gateway-url http://127.0.0.1:8021 \
--lightrag-container lightrag-server2 --gateway-container gateway-api2 \
--gateway-service gateway-api2 --lightrag-service lightrag-server2 \
--worker-container none --compose-file ~/rag-project/stack2/compose.yml \
--compose-project rag-chunk2 --env-file ~/rag-project/stack2/.env \
--draws 3 --compare R0-baseline R3-graph-budget-shift \
--second-judge-model phi-4 --second-judge-fraction 0.2
Never run this file against production without --allow-production; it wipes the store.
(This file asks for reingest:false on every arm, so on a correctly built second stack it
does not wipe anything - the sentence is here because the driver CAN wipe what it points
at, and a typo in --lightrag-url is the kind of mistake that costs a corpus.)
Every key below is in the driver's own whitelist (scripts/overnight_loop.py
ENV_WHITELIST / GATEWAY_ENV_WHITELIST) and names something this repo actually sends:
- LightRAG server env: TOP_K, CHUNK_TOP_K, MAX_ENTITY_TOKENS, MAX_RELATION_TOKENS,
RERANK_BY_DEFAULT. These are what the direct /query retrieval-recall probe measures.
- gateway env (the path Open WebUI actually uses, app/api.py
build_ollama_bridge_query_payload): BRIDGE_TOP_K, BRIDGE_CHUNK_TOP_K,
BRIDGE_MAX_ENTITY_TOKENS, BRIDGE_MAX_RELATION_TOKENS, BRIDGE_MAX_TOTAL_TOKENS,
BRIDGE_ENABLE_RERANK. The bridge sends these as top_k / chunk_top_k /
max_entity_tokens / max_relation_tokens / max_total_tokens / enable_rerank.
How the recall number is produced, with the field names the driver actually sends
(they are the ones app/api.py already posts to /query): mode, query,
only_need_context: true, include_chunk_content: true, include_references: true. It sends
no top_k, chunk_top_k or token budgets at all, because those are what the arm under test
sets; the response is checked for the probe's gold quote. That is what makes this file
measurable: it is the only number in the table that moves when ONE of these knobs moves.
There is no separate 'rerank candidate depth' field in what this repo sends: the chunk
pool the reranker orders IS chunk_top_k, so the depth arms are the CHUNK_TOP_K arms, and
the rerank arms turn reranking on and off rather than resize its input.
What this file CANNOT sweep: the query MODE. build_ollama_bridge_query_payload hard-codes
mode 'mix' (app/api.py:217), so a naive/hybrid/local arm is a code change, not an arm
here. The per-arm 'recall_mode' key only changes the MODE OF THE RECALL PROBE (what we
ask LightRAG for), never what the answer path retrieves - set it on an arm only when you
want the recall number computed in another mode.
Production baseline for reference (docs/05-known-good-config.md and app/config.py
defaults): mix mode, top_k 40, chunk_top_k 20, max_entity_tokens 10000,
max_relation_tokens 10000, max_total_tokens 32000. With 20k of a 32k budget reserved for
graph text, roughly eight 1200-token chunks fit however high chunk_top_k is set - that is
why the budget-shift arm exists next to the depth arms.
Cost: no re-ingest, so every arm is probes x draws x (answer + one /query) plus the
judge calls. On 60 probes at 3 draws that is about 360 gateway queries per arm, minutes
to an hour, not the nine hours a re-ingest arm costs.

experiments.name: R0-baseline
experiments._note: Control: production settings, unchanged. Every other arm is compared against this one.

experiments.name: R1-chunk-depth-50
experiments._note: chunk_top_k 20 -> 50: a bigger pool for the reranker to order.

experiments.name: R2-chunk-depth-100
experiments._note: chunk_top_k 20 -> 100: the depth where a cross-encoder benchmark stopped being the limiter.

experiments.name: R3-graph-budget-shift
experiments._note: Entity/relation text 10000 -> 3500 each, total unchanged: the chunk slice of max_total_tokens grows from ~12k to ~25k, so more 1200-token chunks actually reach the model. This is the arm F10 says to run.

experiments.name: R4-shift-plus-depth-100
experiments._note: R2 and R3 together: the pool and the budget, which is the combination worth testing once each alone has a number.

experiments.name: R5-retrieval-k-80
experiments._note: top_k 40 -> 80 (more entities/relations collected upstream of the chunk pick).

experiments.name: R6-no-rerank
experiments._note: Rerank off on the path the user actually takes. Keep as a placebo: if this arm is indistinguishable from R0, the reranker is not the lever on this corpus.

experiments.name: R7-lightrag-rerank-off
experiments._note: Rerank off on the LightRAG side (RERANK_BY_DEFAULT, which production sets True). The bridge overrides reranking per request, so this arm moves the retrieval-recall number rather than the user path: read it as 'does reranking change what evidence arrives', not as an accuracy arm.
